summary: Three slow days through the abode of the clouds: a lakeside drive into Shillong, waterfalls and living root bridges around Cherrapunji, and a boat on the clearest river in India at Dawki — with your own car, driver and stays sorted.
highlights: Stand at the edge of Nohkalikai, one of India's tallest plunge waterfalls
Walk across a centuries-old living root bridge grown by Khasi villagers
Drift over Dawki's Umngot river, so clear the boats seem to float on air
Watch clouds roll through the valleys at Laitlum Canyons
Visit Mawlynnong, often called the cleanest village in Asia
description: This is Meghalaya at the pace it deserves. Your driver-guide meets you on arrival and takes the scenic road past Umiam Lake into Shillong, the hill capital, where the evening is yours to wander Police Bazar.

Day two climbs into Cherrapunji, once the wettest place on earth. You'll stop at Nohkalikai and Seven Sisters falls, explore limestone caves, and take the short trail to a living root bridge before an unhurried evening in the hills.

On the final day you head south to the Bangladesh border, where the Umngot river at Dawki runs so clear you can see the riverbed from the boat. On the way back you'll stop at Mawlynnong village and the balancing rock before your drop-off.

Pickup and drop-off in Guwahati or Shillong

reviews.text: Great trip overall. It rained a lot on day two so we swapped the order of stops, and the team handled it smoothly. The 3-star hotel in Cherrapunji was basic but clean.

reviews.name: Sofia

faqs.question: Can we start from Shillong instead of Guwahati?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose either city at booking; the itinerary stays the same and the price doesn't change.

faqs.question: Is the living root bridge walk difficult?
faqs.answer: The short trail on day two has around 300 steps each way. Your guide will suggest an easier viewpoint if you prefer.

faqs.question: What happens if it rains?
faqs.answer: Rain is part of Meghalaya's magic. We reorder stops to catch the clearest windows; the falls are at their best after a downpour.

faqs.question: Do we need a permit?
faqs.answer: No permit, but every visitor must register on the Meghalaya Tourism app and carry the e-invite. We'll send you the link.

faqs.question: Which season is best?
faqs.answer: October to April for clear views and calm rivers. June to September is monsoon: the waterfalls are at their biggest but Dawki boating may close.

faqs.question: Can you add a day or a stop?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tell us in your request and we will send a revised itinerary and price.

faqs.question: Is it suitable for children and older travellers?
faqs.answer: Yes — the pace is relaxed and you can skip the root bridge trail. Child seats are available on request.
